seo.overviewTitle: AI Agent Flow & Tool-Calling Architecture (Function Calling)
seo.overviewBody: AI agents execute autonomous multi-step tasks by calling external tools and APIs. AI engineers build agent workflows using the ReAct framework (Reason + Act), OpenAI Function Calling / Gemini Tool Use, JSON tool schema definitions, and loop control guards.

deliverables.title: 1. AI Agent ReAct Loop Architecture Diagram
deliverables.desc: Flowchart illustrating Thought -> Action -> Observation -> Thought execution loops for multi-tool AI agents.

deliverables.title: 2. Tool Calling JSON Schema Specification
deliverables.desc: Collection of tool JSON schemas defining function names, parameters, descriptions, and required arguments.

deliverables.title: 3. Multi-Step Agent Execution Trace Log
deliverables.desc: Trace log detailing agent tool calls, API request-response payloads, state updates, and goal completion.

faqs.question: How does the ReAct (Reason + Act) agent loop work?
faqs.answer: The agent generates a Thought about the current state, selects an Action (tool call), receives an Observation (tool execution output), and repeats until reaching the final answer.

faqs.question: Why are clear tool descriptions critical for OpenAI Function Calling?
faqs.answer: The LLM relies entirely on tool description text to determine WHEN and HOW to invoke a tool; vague descriptions lead to misfires or incorrect argument formatting.

faqs.question: How do you prevent AI agents from getting stuck in infinite execution loops?
faqs.answer: Implement maximum step limits (e.g. max 5 iterations), timeout guards, duplicate tool call detection, and explicit human-in-the-loop fallback triggers.
